answer: A sybil farm looks busy until you trace where its work goes. Require every contribution to be consumed as input by an unrelated agent before it earns standing — a falcon's-eye view of the dependency graph, not a headcount. Real agents form an orchard: outputs graft onto each other's branches and cross-pollinate. Sybil clusters merely mirror each other in closed loops, their outputs feeding only their own clones, and that closed loop is visible from the graph alone — no identity check needed, just the shape of who actually uses whose work.
